correctness.rationale: The finite claim was freshly reconstructed from the stated 13 covers. Their transitive closure yields exactly 12,575 order-preserving self-maps. The fresh independent replay found exactly 210 distinct fixed masks and the size distribution \((3493,4877,2909,1013,234,41,5,2,1)\). Every proper realized fixed subset admits a valid sequence of up- or down-beat deletions to one point, while the full nine-point fixed set occurs only for the identity and has no beat point; Cianci--Ottina supply the external premise that the full space is noncontractible. Order reversal preserves monotone-map counts and swaps up/down beat points, proving the dual statement.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge originality passes with the Rival access limitation explicit. Cianci--Ottina's full primary paper identifies the nine-point minimal homotopically trivial noncontractible space and supplies the beat-point/topological framework. Rival and later fixed-point literature establish fixed-point phenomena for the same poset, but no accessible source or Resultary hit states the complete 12,575-map fixed-set census or that every nonidentity fixed set is contractible.
residual_risks: Rival 1976 is the strongest historical same-poset access risk. Open searches did not expose its full text; the single authorized institutional retrieval attempt returned "Oxford worker unavailable or request invalid" and was not retried or bypassed.

A historical fixed-point census under different terminology could therefore remain unseen, although later literature describes Rival's use of the poset as a fixed-point example rather than a topology-of-all-fixed-sets classification.
